newsitem.title: USA: WSCC, BPA to discuss Intertie power line Wed-Thurs.
newsitem.headline: WSCC, BPA to discuss Intertie power line Wed-Thurs.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) will meet Wednesday and Thursday with a Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) study group to discuss plans for the Pacific Intertie, the WSCC said Tuesday.

BPA is expected to present a plan for springtime operation of the interstate transmission lines, which link the Northwest to southern California, and the study group could accept, reject or request more information on the plan.
Meanwhile, the board of the WSCC continued to review a plan for winter operation of the line which the study group forwarded last month.
A final assessment by the WSCC on the winter plan is not expected until late this month.

If it is approved, it will remain in effect no later than the end of April or until operating conditions, such as the weather, no longer match the winter plan's criteria, a WSCC spokeswoman explained.

If the spring plan is not approved by the WSCC board and members by that time, intertie operations would revert back to the capacity limits put in place last August after two major blackouts hit several western states, she said.
Those constraints have limited combined capacity of the lines to 5,200 megawatts (MW), compared with their rated capacity of 7,900 MW.
Under BPA's winter operating plan, the limit would increase about 25 percent to 6,250 MW.
